story: On September 1st, 2026 the Department of Homeland Security Science and Technology Directorate published its account of an operational assessment of facial biometric image capture, run for U.S. Customs and Border Protection on the pedestrian exit lane at the Progreso International Bridge in Hidalgo County, Texas. Customs and Border Protection asked for the work in October 2025. Six companies were demonstrated at the Maryland Test Facility in early 2026 and three solutions went to the bridge in May, two from NEC National Security Systems and one joint solution from Paravision and AiFi. The account is written almost entirely in adjectives. It publishes no accuracy figure, no count of images captured, no retention period, no deployment decision and no date in May beyond the month. The one hard quantity in it belongs to the crossing rather than to the technology. The same agency publishes a measured monthly pedestrian count for people walking IN at this port, and states plainly that it collects no comparable data on the way out.

claims.text: The account is published by the Science and Technology Directorate and describes work it carried out for U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the Progreso International Bridge crossing in Texas.
claims.quote: The Science and Technology Directorate (S&T) recently brought industry partners to the Progreso International Bridge border crossing in Texas to demonstrate facial biometric capabilities for U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP).

claims.text: The work began with a CBP request to the directorate in October 2025 for solutions to confirm the departure of pedestrians leaving the United States using biometrics.
claims.quote: "In October 2025, CBP approached S&T with a request for solutions that could securely, efficiently, and accurately confirm the departure of pedestrians exiting the U.S. at border crossings using biometrics," said Arun Vemury, S&T Senior Advisor for Biometrics and Identity.

claims.text: Six companies were invited to the Maryland Test Facility in early 2026 for capability demonstrations that decided which solutions would be tested operationally.
claims.quote: In early 2026, S&T invited six companies to the Maryland Test Facility (MdTF) for basic capability demonstrations to determine which solutions should be operationally tested.

claims.text: CBP and the directorate selected three solutions for further data collection, two from NEC National Security Systems and one joint solution from Paravision and AiFi.
claims.quote: These demonstrations led CBP and S&T to select three solutions for additional data collection: two from NEC National Security Systems (NSS) and one joint solution from Paravision and AiFi.

claims.text: The industry partners arrived at the Progreso International Bridge in May and set up for an operational assessment meant to support CBP's planning.
claims.quote: When the industry partners arrived at the Progreso International Bridge in May, they began setting up for the operational assessment that would support CBP's planning.

claims.text: CBP's verdict on the assessment is delivered as an adjective by the director of its Biometrics Program Office.
claims.quote: "We were extremely impressed with the technology and the vendors that S&T brought down to Progreso on our behalf," said Larry Panetta, Director of CBP's Biometrics Program Office.

claims.text: The nearest thing the account offers to a performance result is the statement that image capture exceeded expectations in daylight and after dark.
claims.quote: The image capture capabilities of pedestrians walking through the border exit area exceeded expectations in both day and night conditions.

claims.text: The pace from concept to operational data collection is characterised as a few months and called amazing.
claims.quote: The fact that this went from concept to operational data collection in just a few months is amazing.

claims.text: NEC describes its own two products working outdoors in weather, in a statement from its president carried inside the government's account.
claims.quote: "We were able to demonstrate NEC's SmartID Express and Neoface Express in real-world outdoor conditions and weather, successfully capturing high-quality facial images of thousands of pedestrians a day," said Todd Morris, President of NEC NSS.

claims.text: The director of the directorate's Biometric, Identity, and Advanced Computing Division frames the difficulty of the site in adjectives rather than in measurements.
claims.quote: "It is one thing for a technology to work in a lab like MdTF, but it is significantly more difficult when the tech is deployed operationally at the border. At Progreso, it had to work with limited infrastructure, in a challenging environment, and do it autonomously," said Dr. Cameron Whitelam, director of S&T's Biometric, Identity, and Advanced Computing Division.

claims.text: Paravision describes the joint solution with AiFi as a seamless and contactless biometric experience.
claims.quote: Together, AiFi and Paravision enable a seamless, contactless biometric experience by understanding how people move through a space and helping ensure that only high-quality facial images are used for matching.

claims.text: The only hard quantity in the account belongs to the crossing rather than to the technology, an annual figure for pedestrians exiting to Mexico given by the bridge director.
claims.quote: "Over 1.1 million pedestrians exit the U.S. to Mexico annually, and it is imperative to keep them safely moving," said Bridge Director Marga A. Lopez.

claims.text: Signs in English and Spanish told pedestrians that United States citizens could opt out, on the stated ground that the mandate applies to travelers who are not citizens.
claims.quote: As pedestrians approached the border exits, signs in English and Spanish informed them that U.S. citizens could opt out of biometric exit collection if they did not wish to have their picture taken, since the biometric Entry/Exit mandate applies to non-U.S. citizen travelers.

claims.text: A separate lane was provided for United States citizens who chose not to take part in the image collection testing.
claims.quote: U.S. citizens were provided an opt-out lane if they chose not to participate in the image collection testing.

claims.text: The account names three things artificial intelligence was used to do, building a digital model of the capture zone, watching pedestrian movement, and judging whether facial images were good enough for matching in the Traveler Verification Service.
claims.quote: The partners leveraged artificial intelligence (AI) and other technologies to perform tasks such as constructing a 3D digital environment of the image capture zone, observing pedestrian movement, and analyzing facial images to determine whether they were suitable for biometric matching in CBP's Traveler Verification Service.

claims.text: Testing was also run after dark with external lighting, because ports of entry operate around the clock.
claims.quote: Because ports of entry operate day and night, tests were also conducted after dark using external lighting configurations.

claims.text: The described design has pedestrians walk past cameras for identity verification as they cross, without stopping.
claims.quote: With this new technology, pedestrians can walk past the cameras for identity verification as they cross the border.

claims.text: The account publishes no accuracy rate, no match rate and no error rate for any of the three solutions. Accuracy appears once, as an adjective rather than a measurement.
claims.quote: This combination supports accurate biometric verification while allowing travelers to continue through the exit process naturally.

claims.text: The account publishes no count of pedestrians encountered or images captured during the assessment. The nearest quantity is an unnumbered daily rate inside a vendor's own statement.
claims.quote: successfully capturing high-quality facial images of thousands of pedestrians a day

claims.text: The account publishes no retention period, storage duration or deletion timeline for the facial images. The only thing it says about where images go is that they were judged for matching in a CBP service.
claims.quote: analyzing facial images to determine whether they were suitable for biometric matching in CBP's Traveler Verification Service

claims.text: The account announces no decision to deploy, buy or adopt any of the three solutions. The nearest thing to a next step is a conditional phrase from CBP.
claims.quote: This technology could prove to be a force multiplier and allow CBP to maximize deployment of resources.

claims.text: The account gives no day, no date range and no duration for the May assessment. The month is the whole of what it publishes.

claims.text: The federal border crossing series counts people entering the United States, and the agency that runs the ports states it collects no comparable data on the way out.
claims.quote: The data reflect the number of vehicles, passengers or pedestrians entering the United States.  CBP does not collect comparable data on outbound crossings.

rejected.finding: The assessment took place in Hidalgo County, sourced to the directorate's account.
rejected.reason: The word Hidalgo appears nowhere on the DHS page, which locates the crossing only as being in Texas. The county is carried by c27 instead, where the Census Bureau resolves the port's own published coordinates, and no slide may attribute the county to the DHS page.

rejected.finding: The Dallas item is presented by Daniel C. Comeaux, Chief of Police.
rejected.reason: The Legistar title names three presenters and a claim naming one would misstate the roster.

rejected.finding: The item belongs to the Dallas City Council Public Safety Committee.
rejected.reason: The API field reads only Public Safety Committee. The endpoint is the cityofdallas client, so the city is established and the words City Council are not in the response.

rejected.finding: An annual inbound pedestrian total for Progreso computed from the published series.
rejected.reason: The series has gaps in the twelve months before the assessment and one month reads as an outlier against its neighbours, so a twelve month sum would be an arithmetic on an incomplete series presented as a measurement. The single month the assessment ran is published cleanly and is used instead.

rejected.finding: The article headline as a quoted string.
rejected.reason: It carries an em dash and a colon, is needed by no claim, and is kept out rather than carried into copy where the house rules would tempt someone to tidy it.
